subject: chemistry
title: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct options
List - I (Functional group): (a) Secondary Alcohol (b) C$_6$H$_5$NH$_2$ (Aniline) (c) CH$_3$CH$_2$CHO (Propanal) (d) Phenol
List - II (Functional group reagent): (i) Neutral ferric chloride test (ii) Azo dye test (iii) Ceric ammonium nitrate test (iv) Tollen's reagent test
Codes:
options: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
questions.explanation: A secondary alcohol gives a positive ceric ammonium nitrate test, aniline gives the azo dye test, propanal (an aldehyde) reduces Tollens' reagent, and phenol gives a colour with neutral FeCl$_3$.

questions.q: The intermediates in heteropolar reactions are
questions.explanation: Heteropolar (heterolytic) bond cleavage generates ionic intermediates — both cations and anions — unlike homopolar (homolytic) cleavage, which gives free radicals.

questions.q:
Statement I: Nitrogen in pyridine cannot be estimated by Kjeldahl's method
Statement II: Nitrogen in pyridine changes to ammonium sulphate when heated with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ in Kjeldahl's method.
Read the above given statements and choose the correct answer from the given options.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in the pyridine ring is not converted to ammonium sulphate on heating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$, so Kjeldahl's method fails for it — Statement I is true, Statement II is false.

questions.q: In the preparation of sodium fusion extract, the purpose of fusing organic compound with a piece of sodium metal is to
options: Decrease the melting point of the compound
Convert the organic compound into vapour state
Convert the elements of the compound from covalent form to ionic form
Convert the elements of the compound from ionic form to covalent form
questions.explanation: Fusion with sodium converts covalently bonded N, S, halogens etc. in the organic compound into ionic sodium salts (NaCN, Na$_2$S, NaX) that can be tested in aqueous solution.

questions.q: The sodium fusion extract is boiled with concentrated nitric acid while testing for halogens. By doing so, it
options: decomposes Na$_2$S and NaCN, if formed
increases the concentration of NO$_3^-$ ion
questions.explanation: Boiling with conc. HNO$_3$ decomposes any Na$_2$S or NaCN formed, which would otherwise interfere with the silver nitrate test for halides.

questions.q: A pair of compounds having the same boiling points are
questions.explanation: (+)- and (-)-butan-2-ol are enantiomers with identical physical properties, including boiling point, whereas the other pairs are positional isomers or entirely different compounds with different boiling points.

questions.q: The IUPAC name for CH$_3$-CO-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CO-O-H is
questions.explanation: Numbering from the -COOH carbon (C1): C1(COOH)-C2H$_2$-C3H$_2$-C4(=O)-C5H$_3$, giving 4-oxopentanoic acid.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of [ring with F, NO$_2$ and CH$_2$CH$_3$ (ethyl) substituents — F at C1, NO$_2$ at C2, ethyl at C4] is
questions.explanation: Numbering the ring to give the lowest set of locants to the substituents (alphabetical citation: ethyl, fluoro, nitro) gives 4-Ethyl-1-Fluoro-2-nitrobenzene.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a pair of functional isomers?
questions.explanation: C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$ and C$_3$H$_7$OCH$_3$ are both ethers (same functional group), so they are chain isomers, not functional isomers; the other pairs each contain two different functional groups with the same molecular formula.

questions.q: Resonance effect is not observed in
questions.explanation: In CH2=CH-CH2-NH2 the lone pair on nitrogen is separated from the double bond by an sp3 CH2 group, so it cannot conjugate with the pi system and no resonance occurs.

questions.q: During the fusion of organic compound with sodium metal, nitrogen present in the organic compound is converted into
questions.explanation: In Lassaigne's test, carbon, nitrogen (and sulphur, if present) from the organic compound combine with sodium to form sodium cyanide, used to detect nitrogen (Prussian blue test).

questions.q: Identify the correct statement in the following :
options: n-butane and isobutane are functional isomers
Dimethyl ether and ethanol are chain isomers
Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are position isomers
Ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate are position isomers
questions.explanation: Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol share the same carbon chain and functional group but differ only in the position of the -OH group, making them position isomers.

questions.q: In which of the following, homolytic bond fission takes place ?
options: Addition of HBr to double bond
questions.explanation: Free-radical halogenation proceeds via homolytic cleavage of the Cl$_2$ bond to generate chlorine radicals, unlike the other options which involve heterolytic/ionic mechanisms.

questions.q: A miscible mixture of C$_6$H$_6$ + CHCl$_3$ can be separated by
questions.explanation: Benzene and chloroform are miscible liquids with different boiling points, so they are separated by distillation.

questions.q: Carbocation as an intermediate is likely to be formed in the reaction:
questions.explanation: The acid-catalysed isomerisation of hexane to 2-methylpentane with anhydrous AlCl$_3$/HCl proceeds via a carbocation intermediate; the other reactions proceed by S$_N$2 substitution, nucleophilic addition, and free-radical mechanisms respectively. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH$_3$ - CH(OH) - CH$_2$ - CH(COOH) - CH$_3$ is
questions.explanation: Numbering the chain from the COOH carbon as C1, the methyl branch is at C2 and OH is at C4, giving 4-hydroxy-2-methylpentanoic acid.

questions.q: Mesomeric effect involves
questions.explanation: The mesomeric (resonance) effect is the delocalisation of $\pi$-electrons through conjugated systems.

questions.q: The number of optical isomers of the compound CH$_3$ - CHBr - CHBr - COOH is
questions.explanation: The molecule has two dissimilar chiral centres (C2 and C3 bear different sets of groups), giving 2$^2$ = 4 optical isomers.

questions.q: Meso compounds do not show optical activity because
options: they do not contain chiral carbon atoms.
they have non-super imposable mirror images.
they do not contain plane of symmetry.
questions.explanation: Meso compounds have chiral centres but also possess an internal plane of symmetry, making them achiral overall.

questions.q: Acetone and Propanal are
questions.explanation: Acetone (a ketone) and propanal (an aldehyde) have the same molecular formula C$_3$H$_6$O but different functional groups, so they are functional isomers.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT true regarding electromeric effect?
options: It results in the appearance of partial charges on the carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: The electromeric effect causes complete transfer of a shared pair of pi-electrons to one atom, producing full (not partial) charges, so statement (1) is false.

questions.q: 1.2 g of organic compound on Kjeldahlization liberates ammonia which consumes 30 cm$^3$ of 1 N $HCl$. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is ...........
questions.explanation: %N $=\dfrac{1.4\times N\times V}{\text{mass}}=\dfrac{1.4\times1\times30}{1.2}=35$.

questions.q: Which one of the nitrogen atoms in $H_2N-NH-CO-NH_2$ (labelled I, II, III from left to right) is the most nucleophilic?
options: All three nitrogen atoms are equally strong nucleophilic centers
questions.explanation: Nitrogen I (the terminal $NH_2$ not directly attached to the carbonyl carbon) is not involved in resonance with the $C=O$ group, so its lone pair is fully available, making it the most nucleophilic; nitrogens II and III lose electron density to the carbonyl by resonance.

questions.q: In Kjeldahl's method, ammonia from 5 g of food neutralizes 30 cm$^3$ of 0.1 N acid. The percentage of nitrogen in the food is ............................
questions.explanation: %N = $\dfrac{1.4 \times N \times V}{W} = \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.1 \times 30}{5} = 0.84$.

questions.q: An organic compound on heating with CuO produces CO$_2$ but no water. The organic compound may be
questions.explanation: No water is formed only if the compound has no hydrogen; CCl$_4$ contains no H, only C and Cl, so it gives CO$_2$ but no H$_2$O.
